entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Apollinaris of Ravenna was a Syrian saint and bishop who, according to tradition, spread the unsearchable riches of Christ to nations near Ravenna, leading his flock as a good shepherd and honouring the Church of Classis by a glorious martyrdom in 79 CE. He is notable for his contributions to the early Christian church in the region, which had a lasting impact on the development of the Church in Italy and beyond. Apollinaris's legacy as a champion of Christian unity and his role in shaping the Church's doctrine and practices in the region make him a significant figure in the history of Christianity. His martyrdom at Ravenna also had a profound impact on the city, leaving a lasting cultural footprint in the form of the Apollinaris Basilica, a prominent landmark in the city's historic centre. The story of Apollinaris's life and martyrdom has been passed down through the centuries, serving as a powerful symbol of Christian devotion and resilience in the face of persecution. As a result, Apollinaris remains an important figure in the history of Christianity, remembered for his courage, faith, and commitment to spreading the teachings of Christ to all nations.
